population: Severe SCD with recurrent vaso-occlusive events
note: Autologous CD34+ cells transduced with the BB305 βA-T87Q lentiviral vector (lovotibeglogene autotemcel, Lyfgenia, FDA 2023); betibeglogene is the β-thalassemia sibling and exagamglogene (CRISPR) is a different mechanism.
label: Sickle cell (gene therapy)

engagement.population: Severe SCD with recurrent vaso-occlusive events
engagement.model: Berkeley and SAD humanized sickle mice (syngeneic marrow transduced with a βA-T87Q lentiviral vector)
engagement.note: Lentiviral βA-T87Q reached up to 52% of total hemoglobin in 99% of red cells after syngeneic marrow transplant into Berkeley and SAD sickle mice.
engagement.short: βA-T87Q up to 52% of Hb in mice
engagement.quote: Long-term expression (up to 10 months) was achieved, without preselection, in all transplanted mice with erythroid-specific accumulation of the antisickling protein in up to 52% of total hemoglobin and 99% of circulating red blood cells.
engagement.judgement: FDA clinical review §4.3 names transgenic SCD mouse models dosed with HPV436, 'a related vector encoding the same transgene', so model_filed is true but product_in_model false (BB305 itself was never put into a sickle mouse).

engagement.population: Severe SCD with recurrent vaso-occlusive events
engagement.model: Berkeley and SAD humanized sickle mice (syngeneic marrow transduced with a βA-T87Q lentiviral vector)
engagement.note: First patient: βA-T87Q ≈50% of β-like globin chains at 15 months, matching the mouse's up-to-52%; HbA-T87Q ≥40% of Hb in 35 Group C patients.
engagement.quote: Fifteen months after treatment, the level of therapeutic antisickling β-globin remained high (approximately 50% of β-like-globin chains) without recurrence of sickle crises and with correction of the biologic hallmarks of the disease.
engagement.judgement: Juxtaposed by me: Pawliuk's 'up to 52% of total hemoglobin' vs Ribeil's '~50% of β-like-globin chains' (different denominators; n=1; NEJM paywalled, abstract only). Confirmed at scale by Kanter 2022 (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2117175; HbA-T87Q ≥40% of total Hb in 85±8% of red cells, n=35) and the FDA review (median 45.7% of non-transfused Hb at month 24). registry_date is HGB-205 NCT02151526 results-first-posted; HGB-206 NCT02140554 posted 2024-10-08.

dose.population: Severe SCD with recurrent vaso-occlusive events
dose.model: Berkeley and SAD humanized sickle mice (syngeneic marrow transduced with a βA-T87Q lentiviral vector)
dose.note: Mice were corrected at up to 52% βA-T87Q; the paper set no minimum, and the clinical ≥30% globin-response bar was not derived from it.
dose.quote: Long-term expression (up to 10 months) was achieved, without preselection, in all transplanted mice with erythroid-specific accumulation of the antisickling protein in up to 52% of total hemoglobin and 99% of circulating red blood cells.

dose.population: Severe SCD with recurrent vaso-occlusive events
dose.model: Berkeley and SAD humanized sickle mice (syngeneic marrow transduced with a βA-T87Q lentiviral vector)
dose.note: Group A at ~0.5 g/dL HbA-T87Q had no clinical effect; Group C at ≥40% (median 46% at month 24) resolved VOEs: mouse-scale fraction needed.
dose.quote: HbAT87Q contributed at least 40% of total hemoglobin and was distributed across a mean (±SD) of 85±8% of red cells.
dose.judgement: Weakest call in the entry. The mouse paper reports 'up to 52%' and no threshold; the sponsor's ≥30% globin-response bar came from the clinic, not the mouse. The low end is Kanter 2023 AJH (doi:10.1002/ajh.26741, print 2023): Group A 'peripheral blood vector copy number (≥0.08 c/dg) and HbAT87Q levels (≥0.46 g/dL) were inadequate for substantial clinical effect'; the high end is Group C ≥40% with all 25 evaluable patients free of severe VOEs (NEJM abstract, paywalled). A re-scorer who requires a stated model target should set this to untested.

efficacy.population: Severe SCD with recurrent vaso-occlusive events
efficacy.model: Berkeley and SAD humanized sickle mice (syngeneic marrow transduced with a βA-T87Q lentiviral vector)
efficacy.note: Berkeley/SAD mice showed less sickling, corrected blood counts and splenomegaly and no urine-concentrating defect; mice have no vaso-occlusive-pain phenotype to predict VOEs.
efficacy.quote: In two mouse SCD models, Berkeley and SAD, inhibition of red blood cell dehydration and sickling was achieved with correction of hematological parameters, splenomegaly, and prevention of the characteristic urine concentration defect.

efficacy.population: Severe SCD with recurrent vaso-occlusive events
efficacy.model: Berkeley and SAD humanized sickle mice (syngeneic marrow transduced with a βA-T87Q lentiviral vector)
efficacy.note: First patient had no sickle crises and corrected hemolysis markers at 15 months; by 2022 all 25 evaluable Group C patients had severe VOEs resolved.
efficacy.quote: Fifteen months after treatment, the level of therapeutic antisickling β-globin remained high (approximately 50% of β-like-globin chains) without recurrence of sickle crises and with correction of the biologic hallmarks of the disease.
efficacy.reason: Crises stopped; hallmarks corrected in patients
efficacy.judgement: Dated to the first published agreement (n=1 case report, abstract-level). The pivotal confirmation is Kanter 2022 (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2117175): 'Among the 25 patients who could be evaluated, all had resolution of severe vaso-occlusive events'; Lyfgenia label §14: VOE-CR 28/32 (88%), sVOE-CR 30/32 (94%). The mouse only predicted anti-sickling and hematologic correction; VOE is a patient-only endpoint, hence direction_only. Group A's clinical failure was an exposure (manufacturing) failure, scored under dose, not a model miss.

safety.population: Severe SCD with recurrent vaso-occlusive events
safety.model: Hbb th1/th1 β-thalassemia mice transplanted with BB305-transduced marrow, with secondary transplants and integration-site analysis
safety.note: BB305-transduced marrow in 58 β-thal mice plus 108 secondary recipients: no vector-derived tumors, no clonal dominance; no sickle mouse or primate safety study.
safety.quote: Immunohistochemistry and quantitative PCR demonstrated that tumor cells were not derived from transduced donor cells.
safety.judgement: Open access (PMC4440358), first 100k characters read. Tumors (lymphomas) appeared in all secondary-transplant groups including mock controls; the authors themselves question 'the usefulness of secondary bone marrow transplantation to evaluate lentiviral vector safety'. epub_year 2014 is from the Bentham DOI date stamp (accepted 2014-11-07); the page shows no online date. model_filed false because the public FDA clinical review lists only proof-of-concept studies and label §13.1 states 'No carcinogenicity studies have been performed with LYFGENIA'. product_in_model true for the vector (BB305) though the cells were murine, not the autologous product.

safety.population: Severe SCD with recurrent vaso-occlusive events
safety.model: Hbb th1/th1 β-thalassemia mice transplanted with BB305-transduced marrow, with secondary transplants and integration-site analysis
safety.note: MDS in a Group A patient was investigated: clone carried no vector integration, insertional oncogenesis excluded; mouse's 'no vector-driven tumors' held.
safety.quote: A SCD patient developed myelodysplastic syndrome post-LentiGlobin treatment; we show how insertional oncogenesis was excluded as the cause.
safety.judgement: Scored on the model's stated prediction (vector is not oncogenic), which held: this patient's clone had no integration site (FDA review: 'the pertinent clone did not contain an LVV integration site') and she later progressed to AML attributed to busulfan; the second Group A AML (Goyal 2022, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2109167, print 2022) carried a VAMP4 insertion at 1-7% clonal contribution and was judged 'unlikely to be related to vector insertion'. But no model predicted the malignancy itself: 2 AML in 7 Group A patients plus 1 MDS in Group C (3 of 54 treated), IND hold 2021-02-16 to 2021-05-25, partial hold Dec 2021 to 2022-12-16, and a boxed warning for hematologic malignancy on the 2023 label (https://www.fda.gov/media/174610/download), which attributes the risk to the hematopoietic stress of mobilization, conditioning and infusion plus SCD baseline risk. Under a strict reading of 'or its silence' this cell is contra; the facts are recorded so it can be re-scored. No nonhuman-primate study of BB305 was found (PubMed, top-10 hits reviewed); the FDA clinical review (https://www.fda.gov/media/179352/download, §4.3) lists only mouse studies.
